CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with particular emphasis on the efficacy of the current medication regimen including amitriptyline and the recent introduction of mindfulness-based stress reduction techniques.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for a follow-up appointment, reporting on his experiences since the last visit. He presents with a detailed symptom diary, which outlines both positive developments and ongoing challenges. His generalized anxiety disorder continues to be well-managed with sertraline 300 mg daily, effectively controlling his baseline anxiety. However, he mentions that he has encountered an increase in anxiety spikes, particularly during high-stress projects at work, necessitating the use of lorazepam 1 mg approximately three times weekly.
In terms of insomnia, Mr. Smith reports continued improvement attributed to the amitriptyline 10 mg at bedtime. He now averages approximately 7.5 hours of sleep per night, with a notable decrease in nocturnal awakenings. He expresses that the combination of trazodone and amitriptyline has been beneficial, although he still occasionally wakes in the early morning hours due to anxiety related to work pressures.
The frequency of tension-type headaches has remained stable, occurring about once every ten days, with an intensity rating of 4 out of 10. Mr. Smith has been utilizing ibuprofen 600 mg as needed, and he has also begun incorporating mindfulness practices into his routine, which he believes may help mitigate headache frequency and intensity.
Regarding persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith reports a slight improvement in his overall energy levels and cognitive clarity since the last visit. He describes feeling more energized during the day, particularly in the mornings, although he still experiences intermittent fatigue that hampers his productivity. He continues to take short breaks throughout his workday, which he finds helpful.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Topiramate 200 mg daily (continued) 6. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (increased usage) 7. Melatonin 20 mg at bedtime (continued) 8. Modafinil 200 mg daily (continued for fatigue management)
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. - Neurological: Alert and oriented x3. No focal deficits noted. - Musculoskeletal: No tenderness or abnormalities noted in the cervical or thoracic regions. - Psychiatric: Mood appears stable, affect is appropriate. No signs of acute distress.
ASSESSMENT
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - stable, with occasional anxiety spikes. 2. Insomnia - improved sleep quality; continue amitriptyline. 3. Tension-Type Headaches - stable frequency; continue current management and mindfulness techniques. 4. Persistent Fatigue - slight improvement; continue modafinil and lifestyle modifications.
PLAN
1. Continue current medication regimen: - Sertraline 300 mg daily - Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime - Lisinopril 10 mg daily - Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed - Topiramate 200 mg daily - Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (monitor usage) - Melatonin 20 mg at bedtime - Modafinil 200 mg daily
2. Encourage ongoing mindfulness practices and consider referral to a therapist specializing in cognitive-behavioral therapy for anxiety management.
3. Schedule a follow-up appointment in 6 weeks to reassess symptoms and medication efficacy.
4. Educate the patient on the importance of maintaining a consistent sleep schedule and managing stress through relaxation techniques.
5. Document any changes in symptoms or medication effects in the symptom diary for review at the next appointment.
Patient verbalizes understanding and agrees with the treatment plan.
